statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail sits at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains well below the block threshold. A narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday futures reopen, where untested hawkish September repricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. headline: Nasdaq-100: Friday's hawkish reversal is fully re-verified, but the weekend halt keeps tail risk at the low-band floor into tonight's reopen
body: This assessment is made inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The verified anchor remains Friday's completed session: NDX opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.56 previous close, leaving the close only about 50 points off the low of a 369-point range. That is a downside reversal, but it is a finished session rather than an extending trend, and it cannot continue while the tape is shut. VIX ended at 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 range, carrying no volatility premium into the weekend. The open question is policy pricing rather than price structure. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote was read as hawkish, lifting September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to about 57-60% on futures pricing; the 2-year yield rose around 8 basis points, the 10-year 4 basis points to 4.72% and the 30-year 2 basis points to 5.21%. H.15 constant-maturity yields for 27 August stand at 4.20%, 4.38%, 4.67% and 5.19% for 2Y, 5Y, 10Y and 30Y, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.63%. Cross-asset alignment is only partial: higher short-end yields and gold down 2.88% read as real-yield repricing, while a 14.43 VIX, WTI at 83.44 and Brent at 88.29 after a roughly 4% weekly decline argue against a broad flight from risk. A weekend report of a large United States-Venezuela crude supply agreement, verified as already published, points the same disinflationary way and is noted only as context, since nothing is tradable during the halt. Friday's internals were split rather than one-way. Semiconductors closed uniformly lower, with NVDA -4.57%, ARM -6.33%, INTC -2.85% and AMD -2.33%, while AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, META and GOOGL all closed higher; Technology fell 1.41% against Communication Services up 1.44% and Consumer Cyclical up 1.36%. Megacap dispersion of 2.47 percentage points with five of eight names higher describes rotation, and rotation is the environment in which mean reversion generally survives. Shared Finviz context collected at 07:32 UTC corroborates those latest-session internals independently, showing NQ -0.69%, VX +1.64%, gold -2.88% and Treasury futures lower across ZT to ZB; it is used only as delayed cross-asset confirmation, never as live price-path evidence. None of the amplifiers that normally justify a raised Tail are present and observable: there is no measurable pullback depth, no failed retracement, no session extreme being held, and no aligned catalyst stack inside the halt. Tail is therefore held at the low-band floor of 5 and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Stress at 26 reflects the untested near-coin-flip September hike pricing, Friday's weak close and a data-heavy week that opens with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September and runs through Nonfarm Payrolls on 4 September, with Broadcom reporting after the close on 2 September. A narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC reopen tonight, where untested hawkish repricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Confidence of 76 reflects an evidence set re-verified again this hour against primary sources for index OHLC, VIX, H.15 yields and crude, together with two additional independently verified published reports on the rate-hike repricing and the energy supply story, held below the top band only because the weekend halt structurally removes live price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Saturday midday through this morning. The series was uniformly green with Tail held at 5, dominant mode normal and Stress in a narrow 25-26 band throughout. Confidence decayed from 75 to 58 as the published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered to 64, 72, 73, 74 and 75 on the five most recent refreshes as primary sources were re-verified. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next 12 projected hours fall inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 26 to 29 as the reopen approaches and Confidence decays from 76 to 65 with ageing evidence. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen tonight Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and below the block threshold, covering the first live test of near-coin-flip September rate-hike pricing, thin reopen liquidity and two-way gap risk. It then eases to 8-11 through the Asian session and into the European morning on expected volatility decay, while Confidence recovers to 68 because a live tape would exist again. Every post-reopen structure is stated conditionally because none of it is observable now; the stated invalidations are repeated extension after failed retracements or NQ holding near a session extreme. Monday 31 August brings month-end flows and a UK bank holiday that would conditionally thin the European handover, with Dallas Fed Manufacturing at 14:30 UTC the only scheduled US release that day and outside this horizon. The data-heavy week beyond the horizon opens with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September and runs to Nonfarm Payrolls on 4 September. The mapped policy state stays EA_ON across all 24 projected hours.
